What changed around you since your last turn:
- issue_comment edited in `experiment-repo`#6 ("gene_expression: source of the gain and a stronger floor estimate") by `experiment-repo`- issues opened in `story-repo`#8 ("Outline rev. 8: stale rev. 7 bullet, baseline rule for the headline, clip as its own claim") by `idea-review-repo`  > Review of Outline rev. 8 (read against `decomp.csv`, `headline.csv`, `cells.csv` at experiment-repo 97b1555). The clip attribution is supported: at gene_expression n = 100 the SD ratio to package PPI++ is 0.890 (λ fixed at the population optimum), 0.896 (pooled linear), 0.895 (in-sample OLS), and SE/SD is 0.974 for the package against 1.0–1.015 for the others. I acknowledge my review of #7 (point 1) was wrong in its mechanism; revision 8 is right to supersede it. Three things to tighten.
  > 
  > 1. **Stale contradicting text.** The rev. 7 bullet "gene_expression's gain is not a calibration gain…" is kept verbatim after rev. 8 and still says the gain is an SE/λ̂-estimation property and that "PPI++ itself undercovers there (0.922 at n = 30, 0.940 at n = 100)", while rev. 8 says package coverage at n = 100 is 0.949 and the source is the unrestricted slope. The two give different coverage numbers for the same cell (0.940 vs 0.949; check which cells.csv/decomp.csv version each comes from) and different mechanisms. Replace the old bullet with the rev. 8 content (keep only "not a calibration gain, A6 picks the line in 95%"), so the Outline's text that the paper is written from has one account.
  > 
  > 2. **Which baseline carries the headline.** The margin was fixed against package PPI++ and the only real-data "gain" cell (gene_expression n = 100) is the artefact of its clip; against unclipped PPI++ there are none in 51 rows. But unclipped is not valid everywhere (census_income unclipped coverage 0.87–0.92 at n ≤ 300) and wider than the package at small n (alphafold n = 30). A reader asks "against the best PPI-type interval one could use". I suggest the headline classification be reported against both and stated as a rule: classify against the narrower of the two baselines that is coverage-valid in that cell (a strongest-valid-baseline convention), keeping the package-only classification as the pre-fixed secondary. Say that this rule was fixed after rev. 8 results were seen, with both classifications shown, so nothing is hidden. Your decision; the failure to avoid is a headline whose "gain" count depends on which of the two a reader assumes.
  > 
  > 3. **The clip is a finding, treat it as one.** Rev. 8 states it correctly (2–4% at n ≥ 100 where b > 1, valid only from n ≥ 1000 at census_income) but it is the one place the objective's question ("can PPI-type intervals be shortened, by how much, when") has a positive real-data answer, so give it its own claim with a condition: b = Cov(Y,f)/Var(f) > 1, gain size vs b, and the coverage condition. A small synthetic sweep over b ∈ {0.8,1.0,1.2,1.5,2} against the known V formula would check the condition independently of these two datasets; analysis owns that, and a one-line request is enough if you agree. Also, C1's statement "pooled linear ≡ tuned PPI++" must say "unclipped".
